flagged.evidence: The Statement assumes only “finitely many isometries” but concludes that P_i = W_i W_i*. The dependency def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator defines an isometry by norm preservation without requiring finite dimension, while def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces says adjoint existence is not part of the definition and is guaranteed in finite dimensions. For example, the inclusion c00 → ℓ² is an isometry but has no adjoint: if its adjoint sent y ∈ ℓ²\c00 to z ∈ c00, the adjoint identity would give ⟨x,y−z⟩=0 for every x ∈ c00; density forces y=z, a contradiction. Thus the stated P_i need not be defined. The Statement needs finite-dimensional spaces or an explicit adjointability assumption.
